ledger.note: 1920, 6 April: a hastily convened Constituent Assembly at Verkhneudinsk proclaims the Far Eastern Republic, a buffer state between Soviet Russia and Japan; at first it comprises "only the area around Verkhneudinsk". American forces left Siberia on 1 April, leaving the Japanese as sole occupying power. fx-27: the 250 km circle around Verkhneudinsk spilled into Irkutsk oblast and Mongolia; both cut out, since the FER page has the frontier follow "the western coastline of Lake Baikal" "along the northern borders of Mongolia and Manchuria".

ledger.note: 1921: bridge to the 1921 keyframe (Buryatia, Transbaikal and Amur only). The Far Eastern Republic page names the Maritime Province among its four provinces and says the May 1921 coup set up the Provisional Government of the Priamur in the Primorskaya Oblast behind a Japanese cordon; the Priamurye page says the enclave was expanded only "to Khabarovsk and then to Spassk". Neither page says who held the Khabarovsk krai north of Khabarovsk, or the Jewish oblast, in 1921, so these cells are taken from the republic's nominal claim to nobody rather than given to the enclave (added by fx-27; confidence 1).

ledger.note: 1921, 23-27 May: a White coup by the Kappelevtsy and the Merkulov brothers takes Vladivostok "to break away from the Far Eastern Republic" (Priamurye page: the government "had its origin in a 1921 White Army coup in Vladivostok and its environs"; infobox predecessor: Far Eastern Republic); the Provisional Priamurye Government is established on 27 May (the Far Eastern Republic page dates the coup 26 May: "a White coup took place in Vladivostok, backed by Japanese occupying forces") behind a Japanese cordon. Typed as a split by fx-27 (was a loss of Vladivostok km 120) so that the whole Maritime Province passes to the breakaway state, as its 1921 keyframe has it; a loss to a counterpart that carries a gain in the same year is applied only as that gain.

ledger.note: 1922, 25 October: "The army of the Far Eastern Republic retook Vladivostok"; the Japanese had announced on 24 June 1922 that they would remove all troops from Siberia by the end of October, and the FER "retook most of the Priamurye Government territory". The lands behind the cordon return to the FER; the Japanese occupation of the Maritime Province ends.

notes: No Cliopatria row: Cliopatria draws its Russian Republic / Republics of the Soviet Union shapes (21.5 M km2) over the whole Far East in 1920-1921 and the Provisional Priamurye Government (344,044 km2, 1922-1923) in 1922-1923; the renderer must cut the FER (and the Japanese-occupied Maritime Province) out of them. The Maritime Province joining the FER is undated on the pages (confidence 1); the pages do not date the Priamur enclave's expansion to Khabarovsk and Spassk; the infobox lists the Provisional Priamur Government as a successor although it was a break-away of 1921 (the successor handover is taken as the enclave). The Priamur page says the coup began 23 May 1921, the FER page 26 May. Japanese occupation of the Maritime Province (from 1918 to October 1922) and of northern Sakhalin (to 1925) belongs to the empire-of-japan dossier (occupation events). States other groups or a gap-filler should write: Russian Eastern Outskirts (16 January to 28 October 1920), Zemstvo of Maritime Territory, State of Buryat-Mongolia, the Amur Soviet government. Kamchatka and Okhotsk are not on the pages and are not in the shape.
